summary: Opaque session cookie signature mismatch after external proxy rewrite causing 403s in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403s for console and scheduled-batch workers in their Private deployment after upgrading an upstream CDN/proxy. Impact: Authenticated sessions appear valid in browser but requests arriving at Redwood control plane are rejected with 'invalid session signature'. Environment: Private VPC deployment for FinScale Analytics (prod-us-east). Observed since 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC, coincident with their upstream proxy upgrade.

High level hypothesis: The customer's upstream proxy performs a URL-safe transformation (percent-decoding) on cookie values (specifically converting '+' characters to spaces) which corrupts the base64-encoded signature segment of our opaque session cookie. This yields signature verification failures in the identity-proxy and results in 403s.

Customer impact: End users and scheduled worker jobs intermittently hit 403s and must reauthenticate; batch inference jobs failing intermittently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has Redwood Private deployment behind external CDN/proxy that rewrites headers/cookies.
2) Authenticate via SSO to obtain opaque session cookie (session=<base64>.<sig>), where sig includes '+' characters when base64 url-safe encoded variant is not used.
3) Upstream proxy performs percent-decoding / form-urlencoded decoding on Cookie header, turning '+' to ' ' (space).
4) Identity-proxy receives altered cookie, fails HMAC verification and returns 403.
logs:
identity-proxy[2026-03-10T18:12:34Z] WARN verifySession: signature_mismatch cookie="session=eyJpZCI6...Ab+cD=="
ingress[2026-03-10T18:12:34Z] DEBUG request-id=xyz session_cookie="session=eyJpZCI6...Ab cD==" user=unknown 
customer-proxy-logs[2026-03-09T18:01:02Z] INFO cookie-forwarded: Cookie header sanitized and decoded; removed percent-escapes
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 18:20 UTC - Support triage: Customer update says issue started immediately after CDN upgrade. No config changes on Redwood side.
2026-03-10 18:35 UTC - SRE reproduces locally by sending Cookie header with '+' encoded; shows verification succeeds for original cookie, fails when proxy-decoded to space.
2026-03-10 19:05 UTC - Identity-proxy uses HMAC-SHA256 over raw cookie payload; signature verification expects raw bytes and is sensitive to transformations.
2026-03-10 19:40 UTC - Workaround validated: Instructed customer to enable cookie passthrough (disable cookie re-parser) in their CDN config. After change, 403 rate dropped to baseline.
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - Engineering note: Consider switching to URL-safe base64 or include signature hex encoding to avoid '+' '/' characters in cookie sig; tracked in INT-4122.

2026-03-11 14:00 UTC - Security review: Using URL-safe base64 for signature must preserve same entropy and verify backward compatibility; requires rollout plan and migration support for existing sessions.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10T18:25Z: Hi FinScale, thanks for the report. Can you confirm whether any header/cookie sanitization rules were applied during the CDN upgrade? Also, please provide a sample (redacted) Cookie header from a failing request.

Customer (Marcus Li - FinScale) 2026-03-10T18:40Z: We enabled 'normalize-cookies' in our CDN and updated WAF rules during the upgrade. Attached a sanitized cookie excerpt. Happening across browsers and scheduled workers.

SRE (Jordan Kim) 2026-03-10T19:00Z: Reproduced locally by forcing '+' -> ' ' transformation. Identity-proxy logs show 'signature_mismatch'. Workaround: disable cookie normalization in CDN. Can you try that and confirm?
Customer (Marcus Li) 2026-03-10T19:22Z: Disabled normalization. After 20 minutes, failed requests dropped from ~6/min to ~0.5/min. Scheduling rollback of the CDN setting was successful.

Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-11T09:15Z: Filing engineering follow-up to reduce surface sensitivity. Linked INT-4122 to track product fix. Keeping ticket open until engineering confirms mitigation timeline.

Engineering (Priya Nair) 2026-03-12T11:02Z: Proposed approach: switch to URL-safe base64 for cookie signature plus a feature-flagged verification layer that accepts legacy encodings for 7 days post-rollout. Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/872
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround: Customer disabled cookie normalization at CDN level which restored service. Engineering has an action (INT-4122) to harden cookie signature encoding: proposal to use URL-safe base64 and tolerant verification during rollout. Customer notified of planned change and recommended to keep cookie passthrough until fix is live. Follow-up: schedule canary release of identity-proxy change and update runbook for Private deployments to include CDN cookie passthrough guidance.
